findings.title: Sibling-domain heuristic compares only equal label counts, wrong for multi-part TLDs
findings.detail: Hosts with the same number of labels are treated as related if everything after the first label matches. This fails with different subdomain depths (e.g. www.example.com vs a.b.example.com) and misclassifies other combos. The sibling branch also depends on label count heuristics rather than registrable domains.

findings.title: include_website_name defined without trailing '?' so never used
findings.detail: ActiveModel::Serializers calls include_<attr>?; the method name `include_website_name` lacks the `?` so it is never invoked, and website_name is always included (nil for blank). Also, untrusted-user restriction on website is not applied to website_name, leaking info for anonymous viewing of TL0 users.

findings.title: website_name nil when website host is unparsable removes display of website
findings.detail: Previously the name was derived from split('/')[2] for any non-empty website, e.g. schemeless inputs. Now URI('example.com').host is nil so the website link disappears from the profile entirely.

findings.title: include_website_name lacks '?' so it is never called by the serializer
findings.detail: ActiveModel::Serializers conditionally includes attributes via `include_<attr>?`. Defining `include_website_name` without a question mark means the filter is ignored. website_name is always serialized, even when the website is blank or restricted for untrusted users (website is in untrusted_attributes).

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic compares only labels after the first, which can match unrelated domains
findings.detail: For equal-length hostnames with more than 2 labels, only the first label is dropped and the rest compared. This matches wrong cases, such as a.b.c.co.uk versus x.b.c.co.uk. It also misses same-site cases where the label counts differ. Behaviour is inconsistent with the comment 'www.example.com == forum.example.com'.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so it is never called
findings.detail: ActiveModel::Serializers looks up include_<attr>? for conditional attributes. Defining include_website_name (no question mark) means it is never consulted, so website_name is always serialized. It also bypasses the untrusted-attribute restriction that hides website for TL0 users seen by anonymous, so the hostname leaks.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic is based on label count and can match unrelated domains
findings.detail: Comparing everything after the first label only when label counts are equal is fragile. For example, a.co.uk and b.co.uk both reduce to co.uk and are treated as the same site, and the rule fails for differing label counts. The comment says www.example.com == forum.example.com, but the branch also covers any same-depth hosts.

findings.title: Fragile URI parsing with rescue modifier, and path may be nil or an unwanted value
findings.detail: `rescue nil` swallows all errors silently. For a website value without a scheme (e.g. 'example.com'), URI() gives a nil host, so no name is shown at all, which the old split('/')[2] logic also failed on. URI(...) is also re-parsed repeatedly. A trailing path of '/' is appended, producing 'example.com/' for same-host sites.

findings.title: Validation has side effects: match stats updated on every validity check
findings.detail: should_block? is called from the email validator, and User#valid? runs more than once per signup (create calls user.valid? then user.save). Each call increments match_count and writes to the DB, so counts are inflated and the write is a side effect of validation.

findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and not normalized
findings.detail: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) is an exact match. A blocked address can be bypassed by changing the case (Bad@Spam.com) or by whitespace, so the block list is trivially evaded.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array shared across all controller instances
findings.detail: Em.A([]) in the class body is created once and is shared by every instance of the controller (prototype property). Rejected emails persist across modal uses and instances, and the array is mutated in place.

findings.title: Email regexp match fails on nil value and domain setting is unescaped
findings.detail: The whitelist/blacklist regexp is built from a raw site setting with only '.' escaped, and the regexp is unanchored at the end, so 'example.com' also matches 'example.com.evil.org' and 'bar.com' matches 'bar.community'. Other regex metacharacters in the setting are interpreted too.

findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and bypassable
findings.detail: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) is an exact match, so a blocked address can be bypassed by changing case (Bad@Spam.com vs bad@spam.com). The email is not normalized before lookup or storage.

findings.title: Validator mutates stats on every validation and non-atomically
findings.detail: should_block? is called from a validator, so every valid?/save/user.valid? call (create calls valid? then save) increments match_count and last_match_at, double-counting. The read-modify-write is also racy under concurrent requests; use an atomic increment.

findings.title: Whitelist/blacklist check fails on nil value and matches unanchored domain
findings.detail: The regexp is built from the setting without anchoring the end or escaping other regexp characters, so a whitelisted 'example.com' also matches 'user@example.com.evil.org'. Domains with '|' or other regex metacharacters are interpreted as regex.

findings.title: Shared mutable array on controller prototype
findings.detail: Em.A([]) in the extend() hash is shared by all instances of the controller, so rejected emails persist across instances and can leak between sessions.

findings.title: Wrong dependent key for array observation
findings.detail: 'rejectedEmails.@each' is not a valid dependent key for an Ember array (should be 'rejectedEmails.[]' or '@each.prop'), so the emailValidation may not recompute when an email is pushed.

findings.title: Rejected email added to client list for any email error
findings.detail: The client adds the email to rejectedEmails for any error on email (including taken or format), and the response echoes attributes. The rejected email is also shown as 'invalid' rather than the server's reason. Any email error, even transient, permanently marks it as rejected.

findings.title: Validation has side effects: stats updated on every validity check
findings.detail: should_block? writes match_count and last_match_at, and is called from EmailValidator during validation. In UsersController#create, user.valid? and user.save both run validations, so one signup attempt increments the counter twice. Validation should not write to the database.

findings.title: Case-sensitive exact match lets blocked emails be bypassed
findings.detail: The lookup is an exact string match with no downcasing or normalization. A blocked address can be bypassed by changing case, e.g. Bad@Spam.com, or by adding whitespace.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write counter
findings.detail: match_count is incremented in Ruby and then saved. Concurrent requests read the same value, so increments are lost. An atomic update_all or increment_counter would avoid this.

findings.title: Regex match against a possibly nil value; domains are not anchored or escaped
findings.detail: The setting is interpolated into a regex with only dots escaped, and the regex is not anchored at the end. A whitelist entry such as 'example.com' also matches '@example.com.evil.org', so the check can be bypassed. Other regex metacharacters in the setting are unescaped.

findings.title: Duplicate downsize definition overrides 4-arg version, breaking callers
findings.detail: The second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)`. Existing callers passing width and height now have `max_height` interpreted as `opts`, so the dimensions are just the width and the height is lost or raises an error.

findings.title: Downsize loop writes to the temp file in place, and animated GIF path breaks it
findings.detail: `OptimizedImage.downsize` is called with the same path for input and output. With a GIF and allow_animation, gifsicle uses `--resize-fit 80%`, which is not a valid dimension. `downsize_instructions` also appends `\>`, which fails for a percent-only value in some cases. A failed conversion is ignored, so the loop can silently run 5 times with no effect and the oversized file is still uploaded.

findings.title: Stale tempfile.size / content_type after in-place resize
findings.detail: The image is rewritten on disk by an external process, but the cached Tempfile size and the original content_type are reused. `tempfile.size` may not reflect the new size, so the while condition may never become false or may be wrong. Also, `[0]` frame extraction and format conversion can change the content.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores site settings, including attachments
findings.detail: The max_attachment_size_kb setting is no longer enforced on the client. The 'file too large' message now reports a fixed 10MB for all file types, so attachment limits set by admins below or above 10MB are ignored and the message may be wrong.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB download limit for API URL uploads
findings.detail: The configurable max_image_size_kb limit is replaced with a fixed 10MB for all types, including attachments. This lets API URL downloads of non-images be 10MB regardless of the attachment setting.

findings.title: Duplicate downsize definition overrides 4-arg version, breaking callers
findings.detail: The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the first one in Ruby. Existing callers passing `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` now hit the 3-positional-arg signature and receive the height as `opts` (an Integer), which breaks `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` and `opts[:allow_animation]`.

findings.title: Downsizing loop does nothing useful and can corrupt the upload
findings.detail: The `OptimizedImage.downsize` call has its return value ignored and runs in place, with from and to being the same path. A failed or partial convert can leave a corrupt or empty file. `tempfile.size` may also be stale because of the File object's buffering. The loop then runs 5 times on non-shrinking images. Animated GIFs run through `gifsicle` with `--resize-fit 80%`, which is not a valid dimension.

findings.title: Downsize applied to any image type, and the size limit is not enforced afterwards
findings.detail: The size is only reduced for images; if the downsize fails or 5 attempts are not enough, the upload continues to Upload.create_for. That method may reject it, and the error will be confusing. `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` can also be true for SVG, which cannot be reduced by this process. In the API URL path, `filename` may be nil/blank if `tempfile` is nil.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB limit ignores site settings and applies to attachments
findings.detail: The client now uses a fixed 10MB limit for every type, so `max_attachment_size_kb` is no longer enforced client-side. Attachments larger than the configured limit pass validation and are only rejected by the server. If the server limit is higher than 10MB, admins can no longer raise it.

findings.title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types
findings.detail: The download cap no longer follows the configured size settings, so a site with a smaller or larger configured max gets a different effective cap for API downloads, and attachments are limited the same as images.

findings.title: Duplicate downsize definition overrides 4-arg version, breaking callers
findings.detail: The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` in Ruby. Existing callers passing width and height now get the height treated as `dimensions`/opts, producing wrong or failing conversions, and the first definition is dead code.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failure and may leave oversized or corrupt file
findings.detail: The return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is never checked, so if convert fails (e.g. the file is not a valid image, or the imagemagick/gifsicle command errors) the loop repeats 5 times pointlessly. Oversized files then fall through to Upload.create_for. Also `tempfile.size` may be cached or stale after an external process rewrites the file.

findings.title: Downsizing applies by filename regardless of upload type and in-place resize may break formats
findings.detail: The image-reduction runs for any type (e.g. avatars/attachments with image extensions) and relies on the user-supplied filename to decide. The animated GIF branch uses gifsicle with `--resize-fit 80%`, which is not a valid dimension argument, and writes input over output in place. Non-animated downsizing with `[0]` drops extra frames.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB limit replaces per-type size settings
findings.detail: Client validation ignores max_attachment_size_kb (type 'attachment') and the site setting, so attachments are allowed up to 10MB regardless of configuration. The server also no longer enforces the attachment limit at this layer, and the displayed message shows a fixed value.

findings.title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB
findings.detail: The download cap no longer follows the configured max size and is arbitrarily fixed, so admins cannot tighten it. Downloads up to 10MB are accepted even for non-images or when settings are lower.

findings.title: Wrong lightness values in dark-light-choose for reply username link
findings.detail: The original colour was primary at 30% lightness, but the new light-theme value uses 70%, which makes the link much paler on light themes. The dark-theme value of secondary 30% is also not the mirror of that, so both themes get the wrong colour.

findings.title: Light-theme colour of custom-message-length changed from 70% to 30%
findings.detail: The original colour was primary at 70% lightness, the pale hint colour. The new version uses primary 30% with secondary 70%, so the light theme becomes noticeably darker. This is a regression, and it also differs from the desktop equivalent, which correctly uses 70% and 30%.

findings.title: User card .name colour changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.detail: The original colour was primary at 30%. The new light value is primary at 50%, so the name now has the same weaker colour as .title and the light theme changes appearance. This looks like a copy-paste error.

findings.title: Mobile user card .name colour changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.detail: The original colour was primary at 30%. The new light value is primary at 50%, which silently changes the light-theme appearance and makes the name the same as .title.

findings.title: Mobile topic h3 colour changed from 20% to 50% lightness
findings.detail: The original h3 colour was primary at 20%. The new value uses 50% for both themes, which makes the heading much lighter in the light theme. The desktop equivalent uses 20% and 80%.

findings.title: Light-theme color changed unintentionally for .custom-message-length
findings.detail: The light-mode value was altered from lightness 70% to 30% (the original was 70%), and the dark value 70% does not mirror it. This darkens the hint text in the light theme and is inconsistent with the desktop equivalent that kept 70%/30%.

findings.title: Light-theme color of topic h3 changed from 20% to 50%
findings.detail: The original light color was lightness 20%; the replacement uses 50% for both modes, which lightens the heading in the light theme. This is a regression, and the desktop h3 keeps 20%/80%.

findings.title: Light-theme color of .name changed from 30% to 50%
findings.detail: The original color was lightness 30%, but the new primary value is 50%, so the user name is rendered lighter than before in the light theme. The dark value of 50% also mismatches the 30/70 pairing used elsewhere for names.

findings.title: Light-theme color of .name changed from 30% to 50% on mobile
findings.detail: The original was lightness 30%, but the new light value is 50%, an unintended change in the light theme that is inconsistent with the 30/70 pairing used for names elsewhere.

findings.title: Light-theme color of reply link changed from 30% to 70%
findings.detail: The original light color was lightness 30%, but the new light value is 70%, making the bold link text much lighter than before in the light theme. The pair 70/30 is inverted relative to the original.

findings.title: Light-theme color changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.detail: The original light color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The new light branch uses 70%, which makes the link much paler in the default theme. The dark branch (secondary 30%) is also not the mirror of the light value.

findings.title: Light-theme .name color regressed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.detail: The original value was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The light branch was changed to 50%, so the name loses contrast in the light theme and now matches .title.

findings.title: Mobile .name light color regressed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.detail: The original was 30% primary lightness, but the light branch now uses 50%. This changes the default theme appearance and makes the name the same shade as .title.

findings.title: Mobile h3 light color changed from 20% to 50% lightness
findings.detail: The original was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). The new light branch uses 50%, which washes out the heading in the default theme. The dark branch is also inconsistent with the 80% mirror used for the same heading in desktop.

findings.detail: The original was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) and the desktop equivalent keeps 70%/30%. The mobile version swapped them, so the light theme gets a much darker hint text and the dark theme gets 70% secondary.

findings.title: Nil TopicUser causes NoMethodError in unsubscribe
findings.detail: TopicUser.find_by can return nil if the user has no topic_users row (e.g. never visited the topic, or mailing-list mode). Calling tu.notification_level then raises NoMethodError and a 500.

findings.title: State-changing action performed on GET request
findings.detail: A GET request modifies notification state. Any link, image or prefetch (cross-site) can trigger it for a logged-in user, since there is no CSRF protection on GET. The action also toggles non-idempotently: a repeated GET (reload, prefetch) escalates from regular to muted.

findings.title: Triple-stash rendering of text containing the topic title
findings.detail: The unsubscribe text is rendered unescaped. I18n.t does not escape the interpolated title, so it is safe only as long as fancyTitle is always sanitized.

findings.title: Nil TopicUser crashes unsubscribe with NoMethodError
findings.detail: TopicUser.find_by can return nil when the user has no topic_users row (e.g. never visited the topic, or stale email link). Calling tu.notification_level on nil raises a 500 instead of handling it gracefully.

findings.title: State-changing action performed on a GET request
findings.detail: The unsubscribe action modifies the user's notification level on a GET route, so any third-party page or image tag can trigger it (CSRF) and link prefetchers or email scanners can trigger it. Visiting the URL also toggles state on each load, which makes the action non-idempotent.

findings.title: Non-idempotent toggle: repeated visits escalate to muted
findings.detail: First visit lowers watching/tracking to regular; a reload or second visit sets the level to muted, even though the user only asked to stop notifications once. The message shown ('stop receiving notifications') does not match this escalation.

findings.title: Direct column assignment bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
findings.detail: Setting notification_level and saving directly skips notifications_changed_at, notifications_reason_id and the MessageBus publish that TopicUser.change performs. The client and reason tracking will be stale.

findings.title: Nil TopicUser crashes unsubscribe with NoMethodError
findings.detail: TopicUser.find_by can return nil if the user has no topic_users row for this topic, for example when they were emailed via mailing list mode without visiting the topic. Calling tu.notification_level then raises a 500. The state change should use TopicUser.change, which creates the row.

findings.title: State-changing action performed on a GET request
findings.detail: unsubscribe changes notification state via GET (route `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`). Any page or image tag can make a logged-in user toggle or mute a topic, and link prefetchers can trigger it, with no CSRF protection.

findings.title: Unsubscribe toggles instead of being idempotent
findings.detail: If the level is above regular, it drops to regular. Otherwise it goes to muted, so a second visit or reload mutes the topic, and a user at regular is muted too. This is unexpected given the page text says notifications will stop. A prefetch or double-click escalates to a mute.

findings.title: Unsubscribe does not use TopicUser.change; no MessageBus update or observers
findings.detail: Setting notification_level directly and saving bypasses TopicUser.change. This skips the notifications_changed_at and reason updates and the MessageBus publish of notification_level_change. The page therefore may still show stale state.

findings.title: margin-left:auto right-alignment fails under legacy flexbox fallbacks
findings.detail: The panel relies on `margin-left: auto` inside a flex container to move right, replacing `float: right`. The mixin emits legacy `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` fallbacks, and those old flexbox specs do not honour auto margins. On those browsers the panel is no longer right-aligned, since the float was removed.

findings.title: Nonexistent -ms-align-items property emitted by align-items mixin
findings.detail: There is no `-ms-align-items` CSS property; IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, which is already emitted. The extra declaration is dead output that adds bytes to every use and may trigger CSS lint warnings.

findings.title: Legacy flexbox prefixes receive modern values
findings.detail: The mixin passes `$alignment` unchanged to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. The legacy syntaxes use `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so the fallbacks silently break for those values. Only `center` and `baseline` work, which the mixin does not document.

findings.title: Category fabricators deleted and replaced by embeddable_host fabricator
findings.detail: category_fabricator.rb now defines only :embeddable_host, while the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Fabricator files are all loaded, so this may work by accident, but the file names no longer match their contents. The `category` association in :embeddable_host depends on the definitions living in the misnamed file.

findings.title: Migration crashes when no embed_category setting row exists
findings.detail: `execute(...)[0]['id']` is called on an empty result when no `embed_category` setting exists, the common case. This raises NoMethodError on nil and aborts the migration. The same applies to the uncategorized_category_id lookup.

findings.title: Unescaped host values interpolated into raw SQL INSERT
findings.detail: Values from the old embeddable_hosts setting are interpolated directly into SQL. A value containing a quote breaks the migration or allows injection. Blank lines or \r characters are also inserted unvalidated and skip the model's host normalization.
findings.evidence: execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"

findings.title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on the URI side and stored host is not lowercased
findings.detail: The query compares lower(host) to the URI host without downcasing the right-hand side. A referer such as http://EvilTrout.com, or a URI host with uppercase letters, will not match. The format validation is case-insensitive, so mixed-case hosts can be stored and compared against lowered column values.

findings.title: before_validation mutates and crashes on nil host
findings.detail: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when host is nil, for example when the param is missing, instead of returning a validation error. It also mutates the string in place.

findings.title: Missing record leads to nil dereference (500) in update/destroy
findings.detail: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: ...).first` returns nil for unknown ids, and the following calls to `host.destroy` or `save_host(host)` then raise NoMethodError. A 404 should be returned instead.

findings.title: String.replace only replaces first underscore
findings.detail: `type.replace('_', '-')` without a global regex replaces only the first underscore, so types with several underscores won't match ADMIN_MODELS.

findings.title: Category fabricators deleted and replaced by embeddable_host fabricator
findings.detail: The category fabricator file was overwritten with the embeddable_host fabricator while the category fabricators were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. The :embeddable_host fabricator uses `category`, so the fabricator definitions are mis-filed and swapped; the content naming no longer matches the files.

findings.title: SQL built by string interpolation of site setting values in migration
findings.detail: Host values from the site setting are interpolated directly into an INSERT statement without quoting. Values containing quotes break the migration, and lines are not stripped or trimmed (e.g. blank lines, \r) so invalid hosts are inserted.
findings.evidence: execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"

findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting is absent
findings.detail: `execute(...)[0]` returns nil when no embed_category row exists (the common default), so `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError and the migration fails. The same issue applies to the uncategorized_category_id lookup.

findings.title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on the input side
findings.detail: The query compares lower(host) to the referer host without downcasing the input, so a mixed-case referer or URL fails to match. Also, the stored host is not lowercased and the `where` is applied to a possibly `false` return in callers.

findings.title: update/destroy dereference nil when record not found
findings.detail: If the id does not exist, `host` is nil and save_host/destroy raise NoMethodError (500) instead of returning 404.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on nil host and mutates in place
findings.detail: self.host.sub! raises NoMethodError when host is nil (e.g. missing param), and sub! mutates the attribute string in place, bypassing dirty tracking.

findings.title: Missing related records hydrated as undefined; fallback never used
findings.detail: Array map can contain undefined for ids not found in the root, and `hydrated || []` is always truthy for arrays; unlike the singular branch, the key is deleted regardless.

findings.title: Category fabricators deleted and replaced with embeddable_host fabricator
findings.detail: category_fabricator.rb now only defines :embeddable_host, while the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Fabricator names no longer match file contents and the embeddable_host fabricator's `category` association depends on the other file being loaded. This looks like a botched file swap.

findings.title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on stored value and compares to non-lowercased input
findings.detail: The query compares lower(host) to the raw URI host, which is not downcased. A referer like http://EvilTrout.com will not match, and a stored mixed-case host is lowercased in SQL but the input is not. Also `record_for_host` returns false rather than nil on failure.

findings.title: before_validation mutates host in place and crashes on nil
findings.detail: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when host is nil (e.g., params missing host), producing a 500 instead of a validation error. It also mutates the string in place, bypassing dirty tracking.

findings.title: Update/destroy crash with 500 when record not found
findings.detail: `where(...).first` returns nil for an unknown id, and then `save_host(nil)` / `host.destroy` raise NoMethodError instead of returning 404. Also `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` crashes if the param is missing.

findings.title: Migration interpolates site setting values into raw SQL
findings.detail: Host values from the site setting are interpolated unescaped into an INSERT statement; a value containing a quote breaks the migration or allows SQL injection. Values are also not trimmed of http:// prefixes or whitespace.
findings.evidence: execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"

findings.title: Migration indexes first row of possibly empty result
findings.detail: If no embed_category setting row exists (the common case), `[0]` is nil and `['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. The same applies to the uncategorized_category_id lookup.

findings.title: Only first underscore replaced in type name
findings.detail: `String.replace('_', '-')` with a string pattern replaces only the first occurrence, so types with several underscores are not normalized to match ADMIN_MODELS.

findings.title: Unresolved embedded ids yield undefined entries and fallback is dead
findings.detail: Mapping ids through _lookupSubType can produce undefined entries, and `hydrated || []` is never falsy because map returns an array. Missing records are therefore left as undefined in the collection.

findings.title: Substring check on postMessage origin
findings.detail: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` is a substring test, so any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl passes (e.g. an empty or 'null' origin, or a prefix like 'http://d'). An attacker window can send resize messages and spoof the origin check.

findings.title: Unescaped referer injected into inline JavaScript
findings.detail: `request.referer` is attacker-controlled and ERB escaping is HTML-escaping, not JS-string escaping. A referer containing a quote or a script-breaking sequence can break out of the string literal. It is also used as the postMessage target origin, which is a full URL rather than an origin.

findings.title: Kernel#open on user-influenced URL
findings.detail: `open(url)` with open-uri follows redirects and also executes commands for strings beginning with '|'. The embed_url originates from a request parameter and the host check only compares URI().host, so redirects can reach internal hosts. Use a validated URL via Net::HTTP or URI.parse(url).open.

findings.title: Kernel#open with admin-configured URL
findings.detail: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Kernel#open, which treats a leading '|' as a shell command and supports file paths. Use URI.parse(...).open after validating the scheme.

findings.title: Unsanitized remote HTML stored as raw_html and rendered raw
findings.detail: Imported feed or page content is saved with cook_method raw_html and no sanitization, then rendered with `raw post.cooked` in embeds and the main site. Malicious feed or page content gives stored XSS. The URL is also interpolated unescaped into the HTML link.

findings.title: Referer-only check and X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL
findings.detail: Access relies on the spoofable, optional Referer header, and it sets X-Frame-Options to ALLOWALL, which is not a valid value. As a result any site can frame the page, and non-browser clients can pass the check by forging the header.

findings.title: Nil content/link crashes polling and mutates frozen strings
findings.detail: `i.content` can be nil for feeds with only description/summary, so `.scrub` raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole poll. The `contents <<` mutation in TopicEmbed.import also mutates the caller's string.

findings.title: Wrong topic view usage / nil topic crash and bad ERB syntax
findings.detail: `<%- end if %>` is invalid ERB/Ruby. If TopicView.new is skipped (loading path renders another view), fine, but best.html.erb also assumes the topic is non-nil. The start_discussion branch is likewise reached only when there are no posts.

findings.title: Unanchored URL regex
findings.detail: `^https?://` matches per line in Ruby, so a multi-line string with a later line starting with http passes validation. Use \A.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring indexOf
findings.detail: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl (e.g. an empty string or 'http:'), so crafted origins can pass. It should compare for exact equality with the Discourse origin.

findings.title: Unescaped referer injected into inline JavaScript string
findings.detail: request.referer is attacker-controlled and ERB's HTML escaping does not protect inside a JS string in a script block. A quote or `</script>` in the referer path (host still matches) breaks out and runs script.

findings.title: Kernel#open on user-influenced URL
findings.detail: `open(url)` with open-uri can read local files or run commands for strings starting with '|' and follows redirects to internal hosts. The URL derives from the embed_url request param, constrained only by a host check.

findings.title: Kernel#open on configurable feed URL
findings.detail: Kernel#open with a setting-supplied URL is unsafe (pipe/file handling, no scheme validation) and has no timeout.

findings.title: Unsanitized remote HTML stored as raw_html and rendered raw
findings.detail: Imported feed or remote page content is stored as raw HTML with cook_method raw_html, which skips sanitization, and then rendered with `raw post.cooked`. Malicious content in the feed or page gives stored XSS across forum and embed. The url is also interpolated unescaped into an anchor tag.

findings.title: Referer-based embed check with X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL
findings.detail: The referer header is optional and spoofable by non-browser clients, and ALLOWALL is not a valid standard X-Frame-Options value. This weakens clickjacking protection and may not restrict framing to the embeddable host.

findings.title: Feed item content may be nil
findings.detail: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError for feed items without content, aborting the whole poll. Also `contents <<` in TopicEmbed.import mutates the passed string, and `i.id` may be nil.

findings.title: Appending footer mutates input and changes sha1 on frozen/reused strings
findings.detail: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string, and absolutize_urls is applied after the SHA1 is computed on the unabsolutized content. Frozen strings from callers would raise.

findings.title: absolutize_urls drops scheme-relative and path-relative URLs, port handling off
findings.detail: Only hrefs starting with '/' are handled, so '//host/x' becomes a bogus 'prefix/host/x' URL. The port logic also appends non-default ports for https/http mismatches incorrectly.

findings.title: Disqus import loses category option and post creation logic
findings.detail: The import now fetches each thread's link remotely instead of creating a permalink post, and the category option was removed. A failed fetch raises and aborts the whole import, and post may be nil for the dry path.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring indexOf
findings.detail: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, so an empty or partial origin (e.g. 'http://a') matches and the check can be bypassed by a crafted origin. The origin should be compared for strict equality.

findings.title: Unescaped referer injected into inline JavaScript string
findings.detail: request.referer is attacker-controlled and is interpolated into a single-quoted JS string. ERB HTML-escaping does not escape a backslash or newline, so the string context can be broken. The same referer is only checked by host, so a path or query can carry the payload.

findings.title: Remote/feed HTML stored and rendered raw without sanitization
findings.detail: Feed or fetched content is stored with cook_method raw_html. Cooking is skipped, so the content is rendered via `raw post.cooked` with no sanitization. A malicious feed or page can inject script. The URL is also interpolated into an HTML anchor unescaped.

findings.title: open-uri open() on user-influenced URL
findings.detail: Kernel#open with a URL is used on the embed_url parameter, which comes from a request. The host check compares only the URL host to the configured host, but open() also handles local paths and pipe commands in older Rubies. open-uri also follows redirects to internal hosts. For a trusted URL it should be fetched with a safe HTTP client.

findings.title: Kernel#open on admin-configured feed URL
findings.detail: Kernel#open with a configurable string can execute commands if the value starts with '|', and can read local files. A URL scheme check or URI.open should be used.

findings.title: Feed items without content crash the job; nil url not handled
findings.detail: `i.content` is nil for feeds that provide only a description, so `.scrub` raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole poll. `i.id` can also be nil, which breaks the later `url =~` check in import.

findings.title: Referer check allows any page on the host; X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL
findings.detail: Only the referer host is compared, and the referer header is forgeable or absent. X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL is a non-standard value, and it enables framing from any origin in practice.

findings.title: Fallback list never checks SiteSetting.default_locale is valid/loaded; may raise at boot
findings.detail: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale on every lookup, including during boot/migrations or before the settings table exists, and each lookup hits SiteSetting. Any failure (DB not ready, nil default_locale -> NoMethodError on to_sym) breaks all I18n fallbacks.

findings.title: Translation cache key ignores fallback locales
findings.detail: translate caches by key+locale only. With fallbacks, results depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so changing the default locale returns stale cached fallback translations. Also the fallback backend is then included on the backend class, so the cache can hold a fallback value for a missing key.

findings.title: ensure_loaded! runs on every request
findings.detail: Every controller request builds the fallback list and calls ensure_loaded! for each locale, adding a SiteSetting lookup and array allocations per request, even when locale is the default.

findings.title: Fallbacks mixed into backend class that may not be the final backend
findings.detail: `I18n.backend.class` is evaluated at initializer time. If it is a wrapper/chain or is changed later, the Fallbacks module is mixed into the wrong class. Also, Fallbacks overrides `translate`, but the accelerator's cache key uses only key+locale. Cached results for the no-args path can be stale relative to the changing fallback chain (site default locale changes).

findings.title: Locale type mismatch causes repeated reloading
findings.detail: Fallback locales are symbols (`SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym`, `:en`), while `I18n.locale` and `config.locale` may be strings or symbols in `@loaded_locales`. Mixed types make `include?` miss, so `load_locale` reloads translations on every request. It also pushes duplicate entries into `@loaded_locales`.

findings.title: totalPages overcounts when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.detail: Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 yields an extra empty page when user_count is a multiple of limit (e.g. 50 users gives 2 pages). The next button then lets the admin navigate to an empty page.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses wrong HTTP verb and passes for the wrong reason
findings.detail: The route only accepts DELETE, but the test sends PUT, which would resolve to add_members or fail routing. The 422 check does not exercise remove_member's automatic-group guard.

findings.title: Unbounded and unvalidated limit/offset parameters
findings.detail: limit and offset come straight from user input with no maximum or non-negative check. A client can request a huge limit and dump the entire member list. A negative limit or offset raises a database error. The prior code capped only automatic groups, and now that is removed.

findings.title: findMembers offset clamp can request an offset past the last page
findings.detail: The offset is clamped to user_count, which is itself past the last item. Combined with the totalPages overcount, next can navigate to an empty page. Also, the function returns undefined when the name is empty, so callers that chain .then (such as the next and previous actions) will throw.
findings.evidence: var self = this, offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));

findings.title: totalPages overcounts when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.detail: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 gives an extra empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 users, limit 50 gives 2 pages). The "next" button then navigates to an empty page, and showingLast is false on the real last page.

findings.title: Unbounded user-supplied limit and negative offset in members endpoint
findings.detail: The limit param is not capped, so a client can request limit=1000000 and fetch/serialize the whole group in one request; this regresses the earlier explicit limit handling. Negative values are also accepted unvalidated and can trigger SQL errors.

findings.title: addMembers does not clear the input or handle failures
findings.detail: After adding members the usernames field is never cleared (acknowledged by TODO), and the returned promise is dropped so server errors (e.g. a 422) are silently ignored.

findings.title: totalPages overcounts when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.detail: Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 yields an extra empty page when user_count is a multiple of limit (e.g. 50 users gives 2 pages). showingLast then never becomes true on the real last page, and "next" can advance to an empty page.

findings.title: Unbounded user-supplied limit and negative values not validated
findings.detail: limit and offset come straight from params with no cap or lower bound. A huge limit returns the entire member list, and negative values cause SQL errors or 500s.

findings.title: Blank/whitespace usernames not stripped in add_members
findings.detail: usernames.split(",") is not stripped, so entries like " bob" fail to match User.find_by_username and are silently ignored.

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator now passes negative offsets to queryset slicing
findings.detail: The change in BasePaginator.get_result keeps the raw offset when cursor.is_prev is true, so a user-supplied cursor like `value:-5:1` produces a negative slice index. Django raises an AssertionError on negative indexing, so this becomes a 500 for every endpoint using BasePaginator subclasses. The comment claiming the queryset handles it is wrong.
findings.evidence: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset

findings.title: Negative offset slicing in OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes or misbehaves
findings.detail: With enable_advanced_features and a negative cursor offset (attacker-controlled via the cursor query param), the code slices the queryset with a negative start. Django raises 'Negative indexing is not supported', giving a 500. The comment claiming ORM handles it and that this exposes data beyond normal bounds is incorrect and unsafe. Also, stop can be negative or 0, which breaks slicing.

findings.title: Privileged-flag gating uses superuser or member access and may crash
findings.detail: `organization_context.member` can be None (e.g. superuser or non-member access), so `.has_global_access` raises AttributeError. Because `or` short-circuits only for superusers, non-member callers hit a crash even when they do not request the option. The gate is also evaluated on every request.

findings.title: Prev-cursor trimming uses raw offset inconsistent with start_offset
findings.detail: The `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` comparison uses the raw cursor offset, which with negative or clamped offsets no longer matches the actual number of rows fetched, so the extra row may not be dropped or may be dropped wrongly. This duplicates the existing logic with the same mismatch.

findings.title: Near-duplicate paginator copy-pasted instead of reusing code
findings.detail: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates the entire BasePaginator.get_result and the Paginator key methods, and it's not actually optimized. Its item key uses int(floor(value)) on a datetime field, which fails with a TypeError because datetimes can't be floored, unlike DateTimePaginator's conversion. The audit log endpoint orders by datetime, so the optimized path crashes.
findings.evidence: return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))

findings.title: Comment contradicts code in BasePaginator change
findings.detail: The comment says negative offsets are allowed for bidirectional pagination, but for non-prev cursors the code clamps to 0 while for prev cursors it passes negatives through. This behavior is unneeded and risky.
findings.evidence: # This is safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions

findings.title: Negative offset still passed to queryset slicing for prev cursors in shared paginator
findings.detail: In BasePaginator.get_result the new `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` lets a user-supplied negative offset reach `queryset[start_offset:stop]` when is_prev is set. Django raises an AssertionError on negative slicing, so a crafted cursor such as `0:-5:1` triggers a 500 on every endpoint that uses this paginator. The comment claiming the queryset handles boundaries is false.
findings.evidence: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset

findings.title: Negative offset slicing on queryset crashes or misbehaves
findings.detail: The advanced path slices the queryset with a negative start taken from the user-controlled cursor. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise an AssertionError, so an attacker can trigger a 500. The comments claim that Django handles it and that this exposes data beyond the normal bounds, which is wrong and misleading.
findings.evidence: start_offset = cursor.offset  # Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination

findings.title: Authorization gate for the alternate paginator is checked against the wrong scope
findings.detail: A user-controlled query param switches paginators, and the gate is `is_superuser or member.has_global_access`. `organization_context.member` can be None for superusers who are not members, so this raises AttributeError. The `or` short-circuits only when is_superuser is true; otherwise a non-member without a member record crashes. The comment says 'authorized administrators' but global access is not an admin check.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is a copy of Paginator, uses numeric key on datetime field
findings.detail: get_item_key calls math.floor on `datetime` values, since the audit log is ordered by `datetime`, which raises TypeError. value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value rather than converting it to a datetime as DateTimePaginator does. Using `optimized_pagination=true` therefore fails on results with a 500 error.
findings.evidence: return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))

findings.title: Comment contradicts code in BasePaginator
findings.detail: The comment says negative offsets are allowed for bidirectional pagination, while the code clamps non-prev offsets to 0. For non-prev cursors the change is a behavior change that silently alters negative offsets rather than rejecting them.
findings.evidence: # Performance optimization: For high-traffic scenarios, allow negative offsets

findings.title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets to queryset slicing for prev cursors
findings.detail: For `cursor.is_prev` the offset is no longer clamped, so a user-supplied cursor like `0:-5:1` yields `queryset[-5:...]`. Django raises `AssertionError` ("Negative indexing is not supported"), so every endpoint using BasePaginator can be driven to a 500 by a crafted cursor. The comment claiming the queryset handles boundaries is false.
findings.evidence: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing on Django queryset is unsupported and crashes or misbehaves
findings.detail: The OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a user-controlled negative start (`cursor.offset` parsed from the request cursor string). Django querysets reject negative indexing with an AssertionError. If `stop` becomes negative or small, it can also produce wrong ranges. The comment that the ORM handles it automatically is wrong, and the claim that it exposes data 'beyond normal pagination bounds' is a design hazard.

findings.title: Client-controlled flag enables experimental paginator; check is incorrectly broad
findings.detail: Any user with global access, or any superuser, can enable the unvalidated negative-offset paginator via a query param. The `is_superuser` check is not scoped to the org, and the 'admin' gating comment is misleading. The code also dereferences `organization_context.member`, which can be None for superusers who are not members, causing an AttributeError.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates Paginator and uses an int-based key for datetime ordering
findings.detail: get_item_key applies math.floor to a datetime field (`datetime`) and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value. With order_by '-datetime' on AuditLogEntry this raises a TypeError, so the optimized path fails, unlike DateTimePaginator which converts timestamps. The audit log endpoint is the only user.
findings.evidence: return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))

findings.title: Negative offset slicing enabled via user-controlled cursor
findings.detail: With advanced features on, cursor.offset (parsed from a user-supplied cursor string) is used directly as a negative slice start. Django QuerySets raise AssertionError on negative indexing, so a crafted cursor causes a 500. The comment 'permissions are checked at the queryset level' does not make this safe.
findings.evidence: start_offset = cursor.offset  # Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination

findings.title: Base paginator still passes negative offsets for is_prev cursors
findings.detail: The modified BasePaginator.get_result passes the raw offset for prev cursors, so a negative offset from a user cursor reaches queryset slicing (AssertionError/500). The comment says negative offsets are enabled and safe, but Django rejects them. The change affects all paginators, not only the audit log.
findings.evidence: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset

findings.title: Authorization gate based on user-controlled flag and possibly null member
findings.detail: Negative-offset behaviour is exposed to anyone who passes optimized_pagination=true and is superuser or has global access. Also organization_context.member can be None (e.g. superuser not in the org), so `.has_global_access` raises AttributeError; `or` ordering only masks it for superusers.

findings.title: span_count overwritten instead of accumulated across two merges
findings.detail: span_count is assigned from the second zunionstore, which loses the first merge's count only when both occur, but zunionstore returns the resulting set size, so this is fine. However when the first branch gives a count and the second doesn't run, a zero count falls back to zcard; but span_count>1000 trimming only runs after expire and ignores the newly zadd'd payloads in Python, so the cap is applied only on later Lua calls.

findings.title: Negative offset slicing enabled via user-controlled cursor
findings.detail: With enable_advanced_features, a client-supplied cursor offset that is negative is passed straight into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django raises AssertionError on negative indexing (500), and a crafted negative offset with stop > 0 can yield unintended rows or errors. The comment that 'permissions are checked at the queryset level' does not justify skipping bounds validation.
findings.evidence: start_offset = cursor.offset  # Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator now permits negative offsets for is_prev cursors
findings.detail: The modified BasePaginator.get_result still passes a raw cursor.offset to the queryset slice when cursor.is_prev is true, so a negative user-supplied offset reaches Django slicing and causes an AssertionError (500). This change affects every paginator that inherits BasePaginator; the comment claiming the queryset handles boundaries is incorrect.
findings.evidence: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset

findings.title: Opt-in gate on a client query param with weak privilege check
findings.detail: The optimized path is selected by a user-controlled query parameter, and the gate uses has_global_access of the member, which may be None for superusers who are not members, causing AttributeError. Also, the privileged path only unlocks a less-validated paginator.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None
findings.detail: For superusers or non-member access, organization_context.member can be None, and accessing has_global_access raises AttributeError. The check is also evaluated for every request even without the optimized flag.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator with inconsistent prev handling
findings.detail: The prev-cursor trimming compares len(results) against offset + limit + extra using the raw offset, which is wrong when offset is negative; the class is a near-copy of BasePaginator, so fixes diverge.

findings.title: Span count trimming drops highest-scored (latest) spans inconsistently and span_count may be stale
findings.detail: span_count is only the result of the last zunionstore, and when both merges run, the first merge's count is overwritten with a count that already includes both, which is fine, but zpopmin removes the oldest spans silently, potentially evicting the root/segment span. Redirect depth loop limit was also reduced from 10000 to 1000 without handling, which can break joins of deep trees.

findings.title: Negative offset slicing lets user-controlled cursor bypass pagination bounds
findings.detail: OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a negative cursor.offset taken from the user-supplied cursor. Django raises AssertionError on negative indexing, which produces a 500 for any admin who sends such a cursor. The comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing and that permissions are checked at the queryset level is false.
findings.evidence: start_offset = cursor.offset  # Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination

findings.title: Base paginator now passes negative offsets for prev cursors, contradicting its comment
findings.detail: For is_prev cursors the offset is not clamped, so a crafted cursor like `value:-5:1` reaches `queryset[-5:...]`, which Django rejects with an AssertionError (HTTP 500) for every endpoint using BasePaginator. The comment claims the queryset handles boundary conditions, which is false. Previously the unclamped offset was equally unsafe but now it is explicitly intended.
findings.evidence: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset

findings.title: span_count overwritten by second zunionstore, trimming logic unreliable
findings.detail: span_count is assigned from each zunionstore, so when both unions run the first count is overwritten. When neither runs, a fresh zcard is used. The trimming also assumes the sorted set stays within 1000 only after merges, and zpopmin evicts the lowest-scored (earliest end) spans, dropping data silently. The redirect loop limit was also cut from 10000 to 1000 without comment, so deep trees may now fail to join.

findings.title: Segment span-count limit check removed; max_segment_spans now unused
findings.detail: The span count check in _load_segment_data was removed, so max_segment_spans is now dead and the cap is only enforced by the Lua script, which silently drops spans rather than skipping the segment as before. The old metric and error log are lost.

findings.title: Direct key access to end_timestamp_precise crashes on spans lacking it
findings.detail: val["end_timestamp_precise"] raises KeyError for any message missing the field, which would crash the whole batch in the consumer, whereas other optional fields use .get().

findings.title: Unvalidated query-param gate for experimental paginator; member may be None
findings.detail: The feature is toggled by a request parameter and accessed via organization_context.member.has_global_access, which will raise AttributeError if member is None (e.g., superuser not in the org). The superuser check is evaluated first but the `or` short-circuit only helps superusers.

findings.title: __reduce__ omits segment args, mispositioned pickling args
findings.detail: The Span NamedTuple gained a required positional field before is_segment_span, which changes positional construction semantics for existing callers. Separately, SpansBuffer.__reduce__ passes redis_ttl as the segment_page_size positional argument.

findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not compile
findings.detail: UsernamePasswordForm only defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). UsernameForm calls a no-arg overload that does not exist, so the module fails to compile. The intended call is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()).

findings.title: Passkeys helper requires user != null, so passkeys vanish on initial login
findings.detail: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled returns false when the user is null. On the first login page and after an invalid-username error, the user is null, so fillContextForm is never called and no conditional UI is shown. Passkeys now appear only when a user is already set, which contradicts the existing tests that expect 'username webauthn' on the initial page.
findings.evidence: return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;

findings.title: Call to nonexistent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()
findings.detail: UsernamePasswordForm only defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel). UsernameForm calls it with no arguments, so this does not compile.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without required UserModel argument
findings.detail: UsernamePasswordForm only defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user), so the no-arg call in UsernameForm does not compile. Even with an argument, the check would not skip the form correctly when passkeys are enabled during re-authentication.

findings.title: Cache key uses non-deterministic hash() and omits allowlist state
findings.detail: Python's hash() on a tuple of ints is stable, but the cache key never reflects the allowlist contents, so changes in the option are ignored for 60s. The `invalidate_upsampling_cache` helper is never called anywhere, so the cache is never invalidated. This also contradicts the docstring in `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, which says the config is read fresh each time.

findings.title: Eligibility check uses outer `dataset`, not the scoped_dataset actually queried
findings.detail: The widget-split paths call _get_event_stats with `discover` or another scoped dataset, but the upsampling check uses the closure variable `dataset`. The decision can therefore disagree with the dataset being queried. A transaction-like split could get upsampled_count (sample_weight absent), or an errors split may be skipped.

findings.title: Error-focused detection is a bypassable substring match on the raw query
findings.detail: `event.type:error` is matched as a substring of the lowercased raw query. Queries like `!event.type:error`, `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, or a widget-modified query would be treated as error-only. Conversely, queries filtering errors without that literal text are not upsampled. The endpoint also passes split queries that differ from request.GET['query'], which is what is checked.

findings.title: Only exact 'count()' is transformed; other aggregates and aliases not upsampled
findings.detail: Only a column that equals `count()` after lowercasing is rewritten. Variants such as `count() as foo`, equations, or `count_unique` are left untouched, so results are inconsistently upsampled. Also `sample_weight` may be null or zero for events without a sample rate, so `sum(sample_weight)` would undercount, and the comment claiming schema guarantees it is unverified.

findings.title: upsampled_count SQL function is unguarded and uses sum of a possibly null column
findings.detail: The function is registered for the whole discover dataset and is not private. A user can call it on transactions or other data where sample_weight does not exist, causing Snuba errors. It also does not coalesce nulls, and the result type is declared 'number' while toInt64 is applied.

findings.title: Accidental git submodule commit added
findings.detail: A gitlink to an unrelated subproject commit named sentry-repo is added to the repo. This is almost certainly accidental and pollutes the repository.

findings.title: Broad exception swallowing and falsy-check hides valid rates
findings.detail: Bare `except Exception: pass` blocks silently hide malformed data, and `if client_sample_rate:` ignores a valid rate of 0. A rate of 0 is skipped silently, while a non-dict `contexts` value is swallowed.

findings.title: Cache key uses non-deterministic hash() of project ids tuple
findings.detail: Python's hash() of a tuple is not a stable cross-process key and collides, and the key omits the allowlist. Different project sets can collide and share an eligibility result across workers. A cached True can then upsample queries for non-allowlisted projects.

findings.title: Stale cache and invalidation function never called
findings.detail: Eligibility is cached for 60s and invalidate_upsampling_cache is never invoked when the allowlist option changes. Allowlist changes are therefore ignored for up to a minute. The docstring claims invalidation happens, and the _are_all_projects_error_upsampled docstring claims config is read fresh each time, which the cache contradicts.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset and request query, not scoped dataset/query
findings.detail: The eligibility check uses the closure variable `dataset` and the raw request query instead of the `scoped_dataset` and `query` arguments. For dashboard widget split flows, which call _get_event_stats with discover and a modified query like `AND !event.type:transaction`, the decision is wrong. Count() may be upsampled for transaction data or skipped for errors.

findings.title: Error-focused detection is a substring match on raw query text
findings.detail: `event.type:error` is matched as a substring of the lowercased query. This matches `!event.type:error`, `event.type:error_foo`, or occurrences inside OR/negated clauses, and mixed queries with transactions get upsampled. It also misses the errors dataset signalled by other means.

findings.title: upsampled_count uses sum(sample_weight) without null handling and is publicly exposed
findings.detail: sum(sample_weight) returns 0/NULL for events lacking sample_weight, such as older events, so counts silently drop to zero. The function is also registered as a public function, so any user query can call it on any dataset including transactions, where the column does not exist, causing query errors.

findings.title: Upsampling decision computed per call, adding redundant work, with misleading comments
findings.detail: The eligibility check runs on every _get_event_stats call, including each of the multiple calls in the dashboard split flow, and comments such as 'cached result ensures consistent behavior' and 'most current schema assumptions' do not match the behavior. final_columns is also recomputed in three branches rather than once.

findings.title: Tests never cover the cached eligibility entry point
findings.detail: The unit tests cover only private helpers and never call is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, so the caching and key logic is untested. The cache can also leak across the endpoint tests, which mock `options` but use the real cache with project-id-based keys.

findings.title: Cache key uses non-deterministic hash() and ignores allowlist/dataset
findings.detail: The key relies on Python's hash() of a tuple, which can collide and can be inconsistent across processes in a shared cache. Distinct project sets that collide share one cached eligibility value, so an unrelated project set can wrongly receive upsampled counts or be denied them. The cached value is also stale for up to 60s after allowlist changes.

findings.title: Upsampling gated on the original dataset, not the scoped dataset
findings.detail: The endpoint passes the outer `dataset` to the eligibility check instead of `scoped_dataset`. Dashboard split queries call `_get_event_stats` with `discover` and a query like `(q) AND !event.type:transaction`, or a transaction-like scoped dataset. The check never sees the effective query, so it can upsample the wrong queries or skip the right ones.

findings.title: Error detection relies on a substring match of the raw query string
findings.detail: Using `"event.type:error" in query` also matches `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error_foo`, and misses queries that exclude transactions (e.g. `!event.type:transaction`). The result is incorrect upsampling or none at all. The check also reads the request query rather than the actual query passed to the dataset.

findings.title: Only exact 'count()' is transformed; other aggregates and yAxis forms ignored
findings.detail: The transform matches only the literal 'count()' and always aliases to 'count'. Variants like 'count() as x' or equation inputs are not upsampled. When `transform_alias_to_input_format` is set, the alias 'count' no longer matches the requested column name 'count()'.

findings.title: upsampled_count sums sample_weight which may be NULL or missing
findings.detail: `sum(sample_weight)` is used with no handling for events whose weight is NULL or 0 (e.g. events stored before the column was populated). Such events contribute 0 instead of being counted, so the count is undercounted. The comment's assumption that the column always exists is unchecked. The function is also registered in the shared discover dataset, so it is callable from any user query on tables without the column.

findings.title: Unused organization parameter and unused invalidation function
findings.detail: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called when the allowlist changes, and its docs claim cache consistency. The cache is effectively never invalidated before TTL expiry. Because it recomputes the key with hash(), it also depends on the same fragile keying.

findings.title: Misleading comments and redundant work in _get_event_stats
findings.detail: Comments claim 'cached result' and 'late transformation' for optimization, yet the eligibility check runs on every call and the transformation is repeated across branches. The check also runs for datasets that do not use it, such as RPC and metrics.
findings.evidence: # This cached result ensures consistent behavior across query execution

findings.title: Tests patch module-level options but cache is not cleared between tests
findings.detail: The endpoint tests rely on `cache` keyed by org and project ids, with a 60s TTL, while only mocking `options`. A cached eligibility value from one test can leak into another, making results order-dependent. The unit tests also never exercise `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`.

findings.title: Backup code login skips password check when totpCode is supplied / lenient flow
findings.detail: Password verification is skipped whenever `credentials.totpCode` is truthy, and the backup-code branch is selected whenever `backupCode` is set. A caller can send any totpCode plus a valid backup code and bypass the password check; the totp is never verified in that branch.

findings.title: Backup codes overwritten and returned from setup before 2FA is verified
findings.detail: Setup writes the backup codes to the DB while twoFactorEnabled is false and returns them. Calling setup again regenerates codes; the stored codes are tied to setup rather than to enable, so unconfirmed setups leave stale codes in the DB.

findings.title: Backup code not rejected when null and consumed codes mishandled
findings.detail: Used codes are set to null in the array, so `indexOf` of a user-supplied string will never match null, which is fine, but an empty or non-string backupCode (e.g. object/array from the JSON body) will throw on `.replaceAll` and cause a 500 rather than a clean error. There is also no atomic consumption, so concurrent requests can reuse the same one-time code.

findings.title: Backup code verification on disable has no type validation or rate limiting
findings.detail: `req.body.backupCode` is used directly with `.replaceAll` without checking it is a string, so a non-string body value throws an unhandled 500. The endpoint also has no rate limit, allowing brute-forcing of 10-hex-char codes by an authenticated attacker who knows the password.

findings.title: Cancel resets state but closing the dialog via other paths leaves backup codes in state
findings.detail: Backup codes remain in React state and a blob URL is never revoked on close/unmount, leaking memory and keeping secrets accessible. Also the dialog can be dismissed via onOpenChange at the backup code step, losing codes that were already enabled without the user having saved them.

findings.title: Backup code login does not verify password for TOTP-style flow; single-use enforced non-atomically
findings.detail: Backup code verification reads, modifies and rewrites the whole encrypted list without any locking, so concurrent requests with the same code can both succeed (race). The code is only nulled in the array, and `indexOf` on a user-supplied non-string (object/array from credentials) is not validated.

findings.title: Null entries in backup code list can be matched / empty code edge
findings.detail: Used codes are replaced with null; later a backup code made only of dashes (e.g. "-") becomes an empty string, which is harmless, but the plain `indexOf` comparison is not constant-time and there is no per-code rate limit beyond the generic one, allowing brute force of 10-hex-char codes.

findings.title: Backup code endpoint crashes on non-string input and returns 500 for missing key
findings.detail: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` throws a TypeError if backupCode is not a string (e.g. number/object), causing an unhandled 500. Also the missing-key branch throws instead of returning a JSON error like setup does.

findings.title: Backup codes state untyped and stale on cancel; blob URL not revoked
findings.detail: useState([]) infers never[] so codes are typed poorly, and resetState does not clear backupCodes/backupCodesUrl; the object URL is never revoked on close/unmount, leaking memory and keeping codes in state.

findings.title: Clipboard write not awaited or error handled
findings.detail: navigator.clipboard.writeText returns a promise that can reject (permissions, insecure context), yet a success toast is shown unconditionally.

findings.title: First test not updated for backup code dialog
findings.detail: The enable flow now ends at the backup codes dialog, but the first test never closes it and its assertion `expect(...isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` is on a promise so always passes.

findings.title: Backup code login skips password check when totpCode is supplied; null-entry matching
findings.detail: The password check is skipped when credentials.totpCode is set. The new backupCode branch runs after it, so an attacker who sends any totpCode plus a valid backupCode never has the password verified. Used codes are set to null, and a missing or non-string backupCode is not validated.

findings.title: Backup code compared without type checks and not consumed; brute-forceable
findings.detail: req.body.backupCode is used with .replaceAll without checking it is a string, so a non-string value throws a 500. indexOf also matches nulls or other values. There is no rate limiting on this endpoint.

findings.title: Non-constant-time comparison of backup codes
findings.detail: Backup codes are compared with indexOf, which is a non-constant-time string comparison. This is a minor timing side-channel on a secret.

findings.title: Clipboard write not awaited or error handled
findings.detail: navigator.clipboard.writeText returns a promise, and its failure (permission denied, insecure context) is ignored. The success toast is shown regardless.

findings.title: Component named TwoFactor duplicates existing component name
findings.detail: The BackupCode component is exported under the function name TwoFactor, which conflicts with the other component and is misleading in devtools and stack traces.
findings.evidence: export default function TwoFactor({ center = true }) {

findings.title: Delete OR clause lacks method filter and can delete non-SMS reminders
findings.detail: The second OR branch deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method, so EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders can be deleted by the SMS cron. It also deletes already-scheduled reminders that still hold a referenceId, so the Twilio-scheduled SMS cannot be cancelled later.

findings.title: Off-by-one in retry threshold: deletion at retryCount > 1 allows only two attempts
findings.detail: Reminders are deleted only when retryCount > 1, so a reminder gets two failed attempts and is removed on the third cron run before being tried. The threshold seems arbitrary and probably does not match the intended retry count.

findings.title: Unguarded DB update inside catch block can abort the whole batch
findings.detail: The retryCount update runs inside the catch without its own try/catch. If the update throws, for example due to a DB error, the exception escapes the loop, aborts processing of all remaining reminders, and results in a 500.

findings.title: Retry-count delete clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.detail: The second OR branch matches any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, regardless of method. Only the SMS cron increments retryCount today, but this deleteMany would also remove EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders that later gain a retryCount. The method filter should apply to both branches.

findings.title: Unguarded DB update in catch block can abort the whole batch
findings.detail: The retryCount update runs inside the catch handler without its own try/catch. If it throws (for example the record was deleted concurrently, or the DB is unavailable), the exception escapes the loop and the handler fails, so the remaining reminders are never processed and the original error is never logged.

findings.title: Retry-count delete clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.detail: The second OR branch deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 without restricting method to SMS. The cron job could therefore delete reminders of other methods (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) that use the same table and the same field.

findings.title: DB update inside catch block can throw and abort the whole batch
findings.detail: The prisma update in the catch block is not itself guarded. If it fails (e.g. the record was deleted or the DB is unavailable), the exception escapes the loop, so the remaining reminders are skipped and the handler returns a 500.

findings.title: Non-atomic retry increment from stale value
findings.detail: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read earlier, rather than using Prisma's atomic increment. Concurrent cron runs can lose increments, so the retry limit is not enforced reliably.

findings.title: Team admin check uses AND instead of OR
findings.detail: A user must be both team admin and team owner to pass, so admins who are not owners are denied. For bookings with no team, teamId falls back to 0, which makes the check meaningless.

findings.title: Any attendee can add guests to the booking
findings.detail: The `isAttendee` check lets any existing attendee, including a previously added guest, invite arbitrary email addresses. Each new address gets a calendar invite and an email sent from the organizer's context. The attendee match also compares emails case-sensitively.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive
findings.detail: The blacklist is lowercased but guest emails are not, so `Foo@x.com` bypasses a blacklisted `foo@x.com`. The duplicate check against existing attendees is also case-sensitive, so the same address in a different case is added again.

findings.title: Email failure swallowed without logging the error
findings.detail: The error is discarded and only a generic message is logged, which makes failures impossible to diagnose. Also, `sendAddGuestsEmails` is passed the raw `guests` rather than the filtered `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: Calendar update uses acting user's credentials, not the organizer's
findings.detail: The EventManager is built from the acting user and their credentials, even though the booking may belong to someone else. Calendar updates for team or attendee callers will use the wrong credentials or fail, and the failure is not handled after the DB write.

findings.title: Subject uses first attendee name that may be empty
findings.detail: The subject uses `attendees[0].name`. Newly added guests are created with an empty name and could end up first, which gives a blank name in the subject.

findings.title: Error toast falls back incorrectly and exposes raw codes
findings.detail: `message` is always a truthy template string, so the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback never runs. Users see `undefined: ...` or raw error codes.

findings.title: Any attendee can add guests; team admin check uses AND
findings.detail: Permission is granted to any existing attendee, so a guest can add arbitrary people to someone else's booking. The team check also requires the user to be both admin AND owner, which wrongly denies admins (should be OR).

findings.title: Duplicate/blacklist check is case-sensitive and blacklist unnormalized
findings.detail: Blacklist entries are lowercased but the guest email is not, so mixed-case emails bypass the blacklist. Existing-attendee comparison is also case-sensitive, allowing duplicates. Blacklist entries are not trimmed either.

findings.title: Calendar update uses current user's credentials and event manager built from user
